doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

chapter: Lead trumpet and the rhythm section
title: Lead trumpeter, drummers and Sonny Payne
summary: Lead trumpet pay, and why the lead player and drummer are the foundation of a band, with Sonny Payne as the model.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Was there a difference in the salary between —
The lead trumpet guy is getting more bread?
Oh yes. That’s why I was the first trumpet player. That’s why I am a first trumpet player. And well anyway —
Let me ask you about the relationship between the lead trumpet player and the drummer?

I know, I’ve heard you ask that question, okay? Extremely important. That’s the most important — sorry saxophone players — the lead trumpet player and the drummer are the whole foundation of a band. A lead trumpet player, even in an orchestra or in the President’s band, they set the timbre for the band, the first trumpet player. They set the timbre for the orchestra or for the band. It’s extremely important that you think alike. I’ve played with some great drummers and of course when I was with Harry and my dear old friend Sonny Payne, Sonny — we played really good together. And to me Sonny Payne was the best. And there’s nobody that played like Sonny Payne. And he would read your mind, he would read Harry’s mind. In fact I was just talking to the drummer here — Sonny when he’d be playing he’d be looking at Harry and he was like reading what Harry was going to do. He’d just be staring at him, like this. And if Harry went [motions] Sonny © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
was right there, just like that. And so the lead trumpet player is laying it down, you’ve got to be right in sync with the drummer. Absolutely.
